## Supplied setup


```{r}
broken_mean <- function(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE) / length(x)
x <- c(2, NA, 4)
```

## 1. Recognize the symptom

Run the supplied examples. Identify the warning, the captured error, and the silent wrong answer. For `x`, calculate the expected mean by hand and explain the bug.


```{r}
mean(c("2", "4"))
tryCatch(sum("2"), error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
broken_mean(x)
# TODO: explain the three symptoms and the expected mean.
```


## 2. Repair one function

Complete the calculation in the supplied `safe_mean()` function; keep its checks unchanged. Compare the result for `x` with your hand calculation, then check `c(2, 4, 6)`. Show that the original function fails the missing-value example and the repair passes.


```{r}
safe_mean <- function(x) {
  if (!is.numeric(x) || !is.null(dim(x))) stop("x must be a numeric vector")
  if (any(is.infinite(x))) stop("x must not contain infinite values")
  if (all(is.na(x))) return(NA_real_)
  # TODO: replace the line below with the corrected calculation.
  return(NA_real_)
}
```
